design_name: Silver-Ant Low-Emissivity Argon Glazing (double pane with IR-reflective cavity coating)
inspiration_source: Saharan silver ant (Cataglyphis bombycina): triangular-section hairs that are highly reflective in the visible/near-IR and highly emissive in the mid-IR, giving spectrally selective radiative heat management; translated here in its inverse (winter) form: a spectrally selective surface that is transparent to visible light but a poor emitter/absorber in the thermal IR
domain: Thermodynamics (steady 2D heat conduction with lumped cavity radiation)
physical_mechanism: Why the previous concept failed and what this one fixes: the Rheum concept treated the argon cavity as a pure conductor (k=0.018 W/m/K) and ignored long-wave radiation between the two panes; for uncoated glass (emissivity ~0.84) radiation adds a cavity conductance h_r = 4*sigma*T_m^3/(1/eps1 + 1/eps2 - 1) ~ 3.4 W/m^2/K, roughly tripling the cavity heat transfer (real uncoated argon double glazing has U ~ 2.6-2.8 W/m^2/K, not ~1.2). It also relied on Robin boundary conditions that the solver could not parse. The silver-ant analog addresses the physical weakness: a sub-100-nm silver-based low-e coating on the cavity face of the inner pane (position 3), analogous to the ant's spectrally engineered hair surface, drops the effective cavity emissivity to ~0.04, cutting h_r to ~0.19 W/m^2/K, so the effective cavity conductivity k_cav = k_gas + h_r*gap_width falls from ~0.059 to ~0.020 W/m/K. The window is then modeled as a 2D steady conduction problem over a vertical cross-section. To keep the model solvable with Dirichlet conditions, the indoor/outdoor surface films and the layers are represented as equivalent series thermal resistances: the normalized through-thickness coordinate x runs from outdoor air (x=0, T=T_out) to indoor air (x=1, T=T_in), the top/bottom edges are adiabatic, and the surface temperatures follow from the resistance fractions (R_out/R_tot, etc.). Expected: U ~ 1.3 W/m^2/K, inner-surface temperature ~15 C at T_out = -10 C, i.e. clearly above the room dew point and ~5-6 K warmer than uncoated double glazing, halving heat loss vs. the uncoated unit.

parameters.name: gap_width
parameters.justification: Argon cavity; 16 mm is near the conduction/convection optimum for argon (Ra stays below strong-convection regime for tall cavities).

parameters.name: window_height
parameters.justification: Height of the modeled vertical cross-section.

parameters.name: coating_emissivity
parameters.justification: Soft-coat silver low-e: 0.02-0.05; 0.84 = uncoated glass (upper bound represents no coating).

parameters.name: glass_emissivity
parameters.justification: Hemispherical emissivity of uncoated soda-lime glass (EN 673: 0.837).

parameters.name: mean_cavity_temperature
parameters.justification: Mean cavity temperature for linearizing radiation (EN 673 uses 283 K); ~5 C under -10/20 C conditions.

parameters.name: h_inside
parameters.justification: Indoor combined film coefficient W/(m^2 K), EN 673 value 7.7.

parameters.name: h_outside
parameters.justification: Exterior wind-driven film coefficient W/(m^2 K), EN 673 value 25.
